hypothesis: Generate reproducible pseudorandom bytes from a short seed, possibly a SHA hash or target-derived pattern, and encode the delta from an already-compressed target.
scope: Theoretical assessment and primary-source review only; no compressor/source change, corpus access, search experiment or benchmark.
assessment: Valid as generator-plus-residual modelling for correlated sources; random appearance alone provides no generic post-compression advantage.

representation.complete_cost: seed or reproducible seed-selection information + encoded residual + generator parameters/identifier + framing
representation.promotion_condition: complete representation smaller than unchanged current archive with independent exact restoration and justified computation

mathematical_findings: Lossless compression preserves recoverable information; fewer bytes do not imply lower entropy per remaining bit.
For known fixed deterministic G and fixed output length, XOR is a bijection given S: H(R|S)=H(X|S).
If S=f(X), then H(S)+H(R|S)=H(X); if S includes extra randomness, the joint representation can contain more entropy.

For a uniform n-bit source, a fixed m-bit seed plus l-bit residual can distinguish at most 2^(m+l) targets. Covering every n-bit target requires m+l >= n. Variable-length codes obey the corresponding average uniquely-decodable-code bound; individual inputs can still become shorter.
Independently sampled uniform bit strings disagree in half the positions on average. Similar marginal randomness statistics do not establish mutual predictive information.

Trying more seeds can improve a hindsight residual, but the chosen candidate must be recoverable by the decoder. Search effort is a computation cost; it is not itself mandatory archive metadata if the search algorithm is fixed.
A hash of the undecoded whole target is not free shared side information. A hash does not by itself create a predictive relationship between G(hash(X)) and X.
valid_special_cases: X=G(S) with a known generator and genuinely short seed; random-looking output can have a short algorithmic description.
X=G(S) XOR E where E is sparse or otherwise cheaply modelled and the whole seed/residual description is short.
Seed derived from already decoded causal context, with demonstrated target dependence.
Existing compressor leaves residual source structure or model mismatch that a reproducible generator model captures.
qualification_requirements_if_later_auth: Positive generated-source control, generated-source-plus-sparse-errors control and independent-noise null.
Charge seed, search-winner index or equivalent selection information; no hindsight oracle treated as a codec.
Fixed generator/search bounds and parameters before qualification; evaluate complete bytes, exact decode, CPU and memory.
Use an appropriate strongest existing model/control on identical data, separating payload from archive size.
A negative arbitrary-generator screen cannot prove every compressed stream incompressible; a synthetic generator win cannot establish general real-data benefit.
prior_art_boundary: Source coding, algorithmic description length, codebook selection and predictive residual coding are established; no novelty claim.
